The following summary explains how the Meridian Review (2026 round) decides whether a manuscript is **HANDLED**, **RETURNED** or **PADDED**; every decision must be made as of the 1 March 2026 deadline.

A submission first meets **R1 – Length**: it must contain at least twenty‑two pages; exactly twenty‑two satisfies the rule.  
Next, **R2 – Format** requires either use of the official template or a documented revision history covering three years or more.  

If the paper was presented at a Tier‑1 venue, **R3 – Venue overlap** applies: the presentation must have occurred more than eighteen months before the deadline; exactly eighteen months does not qualify.  

For papers that appeared in an earlier Meridian round, **R4 – Prior rounds** disqualifies them unless at least five years have elapsed since that acceptance; exactly five years is acceptable.  

A **paired submission** (exactly two manuscripts) is allowed under **R5** provided each manuscript satisfies R1 and R2, and at least one of the pair meets R3; both need not satisfy R3.  

Manuscripts submitted to Track D are exempt from R2 but must carry exactly two endorsements instead of any endorsement count; this exemption does not affect any other rule (**R6**).  

An open retraction notice triggers **R7**, which immediately makes the paper RETURNED, overriding every other rule, including R9.  

Figure counts are governed by **R8 – Figures**: a single submission must have between eight and forty‑five figures inclusive; a paired submission may have up to seventy figures but still needs at least eight.  

If a manuscript fails R8 only because it has fewer than the minimum, **R9 – Figure adjustment** pads it to the required minimum and yields a PADDED verdict; any excess beyond the maximum causes an outright RETURNED.  

Finally, **R10 – Withdrawals** states that a withdrawal in a prior round does not count as an acceptance for R4, and it resets the R3 venue clock so the presentation date is treated as the withdrawal date.

The only possible outcomes are: HANDLED (all applicable rules satisfied), PADDED (only the low‑figure case of R9 applies), or RETURNED (any other rule violation).
